newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rift within ETA deepens as prisoners blast killing.
newsitem.headline: Rift within ETA deepens as prisoners blast killing.

text.p: A rift within the once firmly united Basque separatist group ETA deepened on Wednesday when two more of its prisoners openly condemned the weekend murder of a young politician.

Two other ETA inmates and several members of the group's political wing Herri Batasuna had previously denounced the killing of kidnapped Basque town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco. A Herri Batasuna town councilman resigned on Monday over the attack.

"From prison, we raise our voices to demand an end of the armed struggle and freedom for the Basque region," the prisoners said in a letter published in Spanish newspapers on Wednesday. "Above all, we demand respect of the right to life."
Blanco's abduction and killing has been met with outrage across Spain, sending millions into the streets to demonstrate.
The prisoners pleaded with their leaders to take note of the angry response.

Criticism from within the separatist camp may signal it is becoming more divided than ever and possibly heading for a split, political analysts said. ETA, they said, is losing political influence among Basques.

Blanco was abducted on Thursday and shot twice in the head on Saturday after the government refused the guerillas' demand to transfer 500 ETA prisoners scattered throughout the country to installations in the Basque region.
Under the former Socialist government, ETA prisoners were dispersed throughout the country to stop them from plotting behind bars.
On Tuesday, another ETA prisoner, Latasa Guetaria, told state radio the group had lost touch. "Violence and terrorism have no meaning," he said.
Another prisoner went on hunger strike on Sunday, the day of Blanco died of his wounds, to demand his armed comrades abandon the violent struggle for an independent Basque state.
Six ETA prisoners joined a 10-minute silent tribute to Blanco on Monday which brought the whole country to a standstill.
One Herri Batasuna town councillor resigned on Monday and another petitioned ETA to refrain from killing Blanco after his kidnap.
ETA began its armed campaign for an independent state in 1968 under the dictatorship of Francisco Franco who repressed any expression of Basque nationalism.
Support for the group has waned since Franco's death in 1975 and Spain's subsequent transition to democracy. The rebels have killed more than 800 people in their 29-year struggle.
